name: Discord
seo_title: Is Discord Safe for Kids? Parent's Guide (2026)
seo_description: Is Discord safe for kids? How Discord's 2026 age checks and teen settings work, the risks in servers and voice chat, and how to set up Family Center.
lead: Discord is where a lot of children who game hang out: chatting, voice calling and joining communities around the things they love. It brought in age checks and teen settings in 2026. Here's what they do and what they don't.
answer: It can be, with the teen settings in place and you involved. Discord now sorts accounts by age and gives teens extra protections, but servers are run by users, voice chat isn't monitored, and groomers do use it. Family Center shows who they talk to, not what's said.

sections.heading: What is Discord?
body: Discord is a chat app built around servers: communities with text channels, voice channels and video. Some servers are small groups of friends; others are huge and public. Users can also message and call each other directly.
You need to be 13 to have an account.

sections.heading: Discord's age checks
body: Since late September 2026, Discord sorts every account into adult, teen (13 to 17) or unconfirmed, mostly from account signals in the background. Discord says over 90% of people are sorted without being asked. Anyone else is asked to confirm their age with a video selfie, ID or another method, and Discord says providers must delete that data straight after.

subsections.heading: Teen and unconfirmed accounts get
body: Sensitive content blurred, no access to age-restricted servers and channels, messages from people they may not know sent to a separate requests inbox, warnings before accepting friend requests from strangers, and no speaking on stage in servers.

subsections.heading: What it doesn't cover
body: Teens can still chat and call friends and join any server that isn't age-restricted. Age estimates can be wrong or fooled, and what's said in voice chat isn't checked.

subsections.heading: Grooming
body: Groomers join servers about games and interests children love, build trust in group chats and then move to private messages or calls.

subsections.heading: Inappropriate content
body: Servers are run by their users, and moderation varies a lot. Some share violent, sexual or extreme content.

subsections.heading: Bullying
body: Server chats and voice calls can turn nasty, and being kicked or excluded from a server can hurt.

subsections.heading: Voice and video
body: Voice chat happens live and leaves no record, so it's the hardest part of Discord to keep an eye on.

sections.heading: Set up Family Center
body: On your child's Discord, open User Settings, then Family Center, and show the QR code. Scan it with Discord on your own phone and both of you confirm. You'll get a weekly summary of new friends, servers they've joined and who they've messaged or called. You won't see what was said.
list: Check their direct message settings so only friends can message them
Talk about which servers they're in, and only join ones they trust
Show them how to block and report

sections.heading: Signs something's wrong
list: An older "friend" from a server who wants to chat privately
Being asked for photos, or to move to another app
Sudden mood changes, or seeming anxious after gaming
Gifts such as Nitro or game items from people they don't know

sections.heading: What I'd do as a parent
body: Ask about their servers the way you'd ask about a club: what's it for, who runs it, who do they talk to there? Keep gaming and voice chat in shared rooms for younger teens. And make sure they know they can tell you about anything that happens without losing Discord.
list: "Which server do you like best? What happens in there?"
"Has anyone you've only met on Discord asked to talk privately?"
"What would you do if someone sent you something horrible?"

teachers: Discord comes up a lot with pupils who game. Listen for older online friends met in servers, private calls, or gifts of Nitro or game items, and follow your safeguarding procedures. Because voice chat leaves no record, a pupil's own account of what happened matters.

faq.a: You need to be 13. Since September 2026, accounts identified as teens get extra protections.
Yes. Since late September 2026, Discord sorts accounts into adult, teen or unconfirmed, mostly automatically. Some people are asked for a video selfie, ID or another check.
No. Family Center gives a weekly summary of new friends, servers joined and who your child has messaged or called, but not the content.
It's the riskiest part, because it's live and leaves no record. For younger teens, keep voice chat in shared rooms and talk about who they're calling.

help: Worried about a child right now? Childline is free and confidential on [0800 1111](tel:08001111), any time. Report suspected grooming to [CEOP](https://www.ceop.police.uk/). You are not alone.
